title: Technically a Breakout, But It Could Have Been Worse
summary:
Technically a Breakout, But It Could Have Been Worse 

             
             
            10yr yields closed just under 4.74 at the end of July and just over 4.75% today. That's the highest close since January 2025 which, at first glance, sounds pretty gloomy. But it's worth noting that several days have ended just a bp or two below today's levels. In other words, it was ultimately a small, incremental bump. Perhaps more importantly, it was not-at-all out of character with respect to the prevailing trend.

title: Highest Mortgage Rates in Over a Year, But Just Barely
summary: Bonds lost ground today, largely due to mechanical, month-end trading (i.e. not due to economic data, inflation, or news headlines). When bonds lose ground, rates rise, all else equal.  Mortgage rates were already fairly close to longer-term highs last week. Today's increase was just enough to nudge the average top-tier 30yr fixed rate to 6.87%--the highest since June 2025. While that sounds fairly gloomy, the average borrower wouldn't see any difference from those seen on July 23rd, 2026.  [thirtyyearmortgagerates]

title: Month-End Trading Taking a Toll
summary: Bonds were actually a hair stronger at the open, but quickly tanked just after 8am. The nature of said tankage is strongly suggestive of month-end positioning. While it's true oil prices are higher than Friday, the spike in bond yields didn't correlate in a manner typically consistent with oil being the driver. Also, there is a relatively sharp move underway in the yield curve (i.e. 2yr yields remain unchanged while 10yr yields are 5+ bps higher). Heavy curve trading in the absence of obvious catalysts and related market correlation all but confirm "month-end trading" (unless there's a huge corporate bond announcement that we missed).

title: Informed Names Daniel Sogorka CEO, Eyes Mortgage Expansion
summary: Informed, the AI fraud-detection platform behind more than $350 billion in automated auto loan originations, has named Daniel Sogorka as CEO. His résumé has nothing to do with cars.Sogorka spent two decades in mortgage leadership at Black Knight/ICE, ServiceLink/FNF, Sagent, and Rocket Pro. Informed built its business entirely on auto lending, serving eight of the top 10 U.S. auto lenders. The company says Sogorka will scale the business and expand "beyond auto lending into adjacent verticals." No mortgage customer or product has been named. But a fraud platform with zero mortgage customers just hired a CEO with zero auto-lending experience — that's the tell.
